messages:
raj: Hey team — I'm getting a 413 when calling /v1/rerank. Error body just says "request entity too large". No clue which field exceeded limits. I can repro and paste the payload if helpful.

raj: Curl I used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d @payload.json
```

raj: payload.json (trimmed to show shape):
```
{
  "query": """Very long user query (~3k chars) ...""",
  "documents": [
    {"id":"d1","text":"... ~900 chars ..."},
    {"id":"d2","text":"... ~700 chars ..."},
    // total ~1200 docs in full payload
  ]
}
```

emma: thanks for the repro, raj. A few quick questions: is this the hosted API or a Dedicated instance? also which SDK/version?

raj: Hosted. Using JS SDK v0.9.1 but hit same with direct curl. This only started after we bumped doc set size from 400 -> 1200.

emma: ok that helps. Short answer: you're exceeding our combined request size limits (we enforce both per-doc length and total request token/char budget). The 413 currently comes back as a generic "request entity too large" which I agree is unhelpful.

emma: workaround options:
• Reduce number of docs per rerank call (stream/re-rank in batches of ~200)
• Truncate long query text to < 512 tokens before rerank (use a tokeniser — see snippet)
• Send a smaller candidate set (do coarse filtering/embedding search first, then rerank top-K)

emma: quick token-check snippet (python + tiktoken):
```py
from tiktoken import encoding_for_model
enc = encoding_for_model('redwood-embed-1')  # pick encoding close to model
def count_tokens(s):
    return len(enc.encode(s))

q_tokens = count_tokens(query)
doc_tokens = sum(count_tokens(d['text']) for d in docs)
print('query', q_tokens, 'docs', doc_tokens, 'total', q_tokens + doc_tokens)
```

raj: thanks — ran that. total tokens ~ 78k. Oof. What's the exact limit? The docs mention "request size limits" but not numbers.

alex: chiming in from eng. Current hosted hard limits (short term) are: 65,536 total tokens per rerank request across query+docs, max 1,024 tokens per individual doc, and a soft limit of 512 docs. Those numbers are in our internal policy but we should expose them in the public error payload. Filed RUN-7648 to return a 413 with JSON: {"error":"payload too large", "limit":{...}, "field":"documents"}.

alex: repro tip: you can simulate with a smaller set by duplicating a ~1k-char doc until you hit the threshold. We added a small test harness internally:
```bash
python tests/rerank_payload_generator.py --doc-size 900 --count 600
```

emma: actionable next steps for you, raj:
1) batch rerank: send docs in chunks of ~200 and merge scores client-side
2) preflight token check using the snippet above and short-circuit with a helpful client error if over limit
3) consider reducing per-doc size (summary/truncate) or move prefiltering into embedding search to only send top candidates for rerank

raj: batching seems doable. One follow-up: can the API warn when a single doc is over the per-doc cap (1,024 tokens) versus total? Right now we only get the 413 and have to guess.

alex: yes — planned fix in RUN-7648 will include "field" and numeric "limit" in the response. In the medium term we're also adding a Usage/Error dashboard widget in Console to show recent 413s and which limit was hit.

triage-bot: Ticket created #SUP-11234 linking to RUN-7648. Assigned to eng-infra.

emma: I'll send a short KB explaining how to chunk candidates + sample JS preflight. Paste of JS preflight (node + npm package example):
```js
// npm: @redwood/token-utils (internal helper)
const {estimateTokens} = require('@redwood/token-utils');
function needsChunking(query, docs){
  const q = estimateTokens(query);
  const d = docs.reduce((s,x)=>s+estimateTokens(x.text),0);
  return (q + d) > 65536 || docs.length > 512;
}
```

raj: awesome — that should do it for now. Once RUN-7648 lands, please ping me so we can remove the fragile client-side checks. Thanks :pray:

emma: will do. marking this thread resolved for support — escalate if you still hit issues after batching. :thumbsup:
